title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Jordan Li
description: Context: customer workloads show increased tail latency and request starvation during mixed short/long sequence traffic in the continuous batcher. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, introduce starvation prevention heuristics, and add conservative timeouts to unblock stuck requests. Changes: 1) Adaptive queueing window: replace fixed window with a latency-aware adaptive window that expands/contracts based on observed P95 token service time and current queue depth, reducing tail queuing for short requests. 2) Fairness weighting: implement a two-tier priority scheme that decays weight for long-running KV-cache-heavy requests while preserving throughput for high-QPS short requests; weights are configurable per-model and per-route. 3) Starvation prevention: add per-client starvation counters and a periodic boost token that guarantees service for requests delayed beyond a configurable threshold. 4) Conservative timeouts and fast-path preemption: add a configurable per-request soft timeout (for scheduling only) that triggers preemption/fallback to a compatible variant; hard timeouts remain upstream. 5) Observability and telemetry: new scheduler metrics (queue_depth_by_weight, starvation_events, adaptive_window_size, preemption_count) plus dashboards and trace spans. 6) Integration: ensure scheduler tuning cooperates with KV cache eviction policies and does not amplify cache misses; added cache-aware scheduling hints. Motivation: reduce 99th/99.9th latency regressions seen in internal canary tests and customer incidents (SUP-887) without sacrificing overall throughput. Testing: unit tests for scheduling policy transitions and starvation counter edge cases; e2e perf harness run using perf-canary workloads (mixed short chat + long generation) showing median latency stable, P95 reduced by ~18%, P99 reduced by ~27%, overall throughput change within +/-3% for steady-state. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated by continuous-batcher.scheduler.v2 with default off; staged rollout to Dedicated and Hosted regions with canary traffic, monitor new metrics and error budgets, automatic rollback if starvation_events exceed threshold. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked to ENG-4128 - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added to perf-canary job - [x] Docs for new scheduler knobs - [x] Telemetry dashboards created - [x] Feature flag gating implementation - [x] Linear tasks updated. Risks: scheduling misconfiguration could increase tail latency for some long-tail workloads—mitigated by conservative defaults and per-route overrides. Release notes: improves continuous-batcher fairness and reduces request starvation and tail latency; introduces new scheduler knobs and metrics for tuning.

review_conversation: Aisha Patel: Nice work—can you explain why we pick soft timeouts at scheduling layer versus relying on upstream hard timeouts?

Jordan Li: Soft timeouts are a scheduling signal only; they let the scheduler preempt or route to a compatible variant before the upstream hard timeout, preventing wasted GPU cycles and reducing queue head blocking.
Miguel Santos: Requesting a test for the starvation counter wrap-around edge case when client IDs are recycled.
Jordan Li: Added a unit test (scheduler_test.go:TestStarvationCounterWrap) and a guard that keys counters by client-session id when available.
Yuki Tanaka: Metrics look good; rename queue_depth_by_weight -> queue_depth_weighted to match naming standards and add tag for model_family.
Jordan Li: Renamed metric and added model_family tag in metric_definitions.yaml and dashboard queries.
Aisha Patel: Can we have a safe default for fairness weights that won't regress customer A (high long-read workloads)?
Jordan Li: Yes—defaults are conservative: long requests get a minor decay (0.85) and boost tokens are enabled only after 50ms of wait; we documented per-route overrides in docs.
Miguel Santos: CI perf-run showed a flaky test (SchedulerAdaptiveTest) on GPU emulation node; looks like a timing assumption.
Jordan Li: Fixed test to use event-driven signaling instead of sleeps; re-ran perf-canary and updated commit e1f4c33 with the fix.
